leads.candidate: Schwarze Maulbeere an der Liebfrauenschule (Black mulberry, Morus nigra)
leads.reason: Facts look strong (WebSearch summary: ND entry 017, ~200+ years old, girth 3.31m, height 12m, planted ~1760, stands beside the grave of Goethe's mother Catharina Elisabeth Goethe who was buried there in 1808) but every source found describes it as standing 'auf dem Schulhof' (on the schoolyard) of the Liebfrauenschule. Hard rule 10's school test requires real evidence the grounds are genuinely open (a public path, a churchyard the school merely borders, stated weekend access) before a school-ground tree ships, and no source fetched this pass stated that. The Goethe grave connection suggests it may actually be in or beside the adjoining Liebfrauenkirche churchyard rather than a closed schoolyard proper, which would pass, but this needs a source that says so explicitly, not an inference. Do not ship without that evidence. All numeric claims here also came only from a WebSearch summary, never a directly-fetched page, so they need re-confirming too.

leads.candidate: Zwei Ginkgobaeume im Schlossgarten Rumpenheim, Offenbach (Q119289494)
leads.reason: 2026-10-18. Male and female ginkgo in the Rumpenheim palace garden, ND per 1979 survey; the ND list shows two near-identical entries (50.1321, 8.8013 and 8.8019). Palace garden access not checked. Four slender Lombardy oaks stood there in 1979, only one remained as ND by 2015 (FR article). Not pursued: no age or measurement. 2026-10-22 verify pass (as frk_022) then write pass: NOT written, fails the findable rule (no confirmed pin, a palace park is not a small site, the CC0 Commons photos by Karsten Ratzke of 2020-10-28 'Rumpenheim, Schlossgarten, Ginko 1/2' are camera positions, trunk identity unproven). Verify notes: The city register via the Wikipedia ND list carries ginkgos in the Rumpenheim Schlossgarten as two listings, each one male and one female, at 50.1321 8.8013 and 50.1321 8.8019 (about 40 m apart). No age, girth or height in any fetched source. Two Commons CC0 photographs by Karsten Ratzke dated 2020-10-28, 'Rumpenheim, Schlossgarten, Ginko 1' (camera 50.132269 8.802292) and 'Ginko 2' (camera 50.132225 8.801444); camera positions are not tree fixes, so the pin stays approximate and trunk identity is unproven. Alive: 2020 photos only, flagged. Park context from the city's page: English landscape garden of the 1780s east of the former summer residence of the Landgraves of Hesse-Kassel, praised by Hirschfeld (1779-85) for its catalpas; the city says the tree stock is over-aged. Four slender Lombardy-type oaks stood here in 1979, only one remains as ND (FR 2015). Do not claim an age. Weak candidate. Sources: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkmale_in_Offenbach_am_Main; https://www.offenbach.de/gaeste/sehenswert/parks/schlosspark.php; https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Rumpenheim,_Schlossgarten,_Ginko_2.jpg

leads.candidate: Enkheimer Alteichen, oldest single stem at the Nachtigallenweg (Bergen-Enkheim)
leads.reason: 2026-10-19. Citizen survey 2016 (Kaltenborn, tape at 1.30 m): 78 oaks over 3 m girth; thickest single stem 4.46 m, about 35 m, germinated about 1670 by the girth x 0.8 formula (de.wikipedia 'Enkheimer Alteichen'). FNP 2016-10-25 (fetched) independently gives 4.46 m for the thickest of 51 oaks then found and says it stands 'tief im Wald'; a Wikipedia photo caption says 4.30 m, so figure disputed. Commons photos by Kaltolaf (CC BY-SA 4.0, 2016-06-12) have no geotag, so which trunk is unproven. Citizen survey, no official register, none of the 78 is a Naturdenkmal except the Berger Warte oak (frk_019). Not delivered: no individual pin, no photo that settles the trunk. Survey coordinates: Nachtigallenweg 50.15346,8.78001; Wagenweg 50.15656,8.78097 (five trees 250 to 280 years at 50 m spacing, a walkable row); Gaenseweiher 50.14729,8.79164; Dammweg/Postweg 50.14765,8.76919 (six trees, easy from the main path, Waldrastplatz). A GPS fix at the Nachtigallenweg tree would settle it.
